risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns: operations are closely linked to defence procurement timelines, naval project execution schedules and government spending priorities, and delays in approvals, project execution or procurement cycles may impact order inflows and revenue recognition. Mitigation cited is strengthening long-term relationships within the defence ecosystem while expanding execution capabilities across specialised naval applications - it does not reduce the underlying single-customer-ecosystem dependence.

Board risk table flags 'Strategic Sector Shifts' - rapid changes in Indian Defence procurement policies or technical specifications for naval platforms - which can strand qualification work in a business where approval cycles are long. Mitigation is active R&D and closer collaboration with defence laboratories to stay aligned.
risks.risk: Rapid shifts in Indian defence procurement policy and naval technical specifications

risks.note: MD&A: the industry continues to experience volatility in refrigerant prices driven by global supply-and-demand imbalances, and supply chain disruptions and component shortages can directly impact procurement timelines and project deliveries - i.e. it hits both margin and delivery schedules. risks.risk: Volatile refrigerant pricing and component supply-chain pressure

risks.note: Board risk table rates 'Supply Chain Continuity' as High priority: reliance on specialized raw materials such as high-grade alloys or electronic controllers can lead to production delays. currentContext.expansion: FY26 was the company's first major capacity-addition year. During the financial year SRL incurred significant capital expenditure primarily towards establishing a new manufacturing facility, with the stated objective of enhancing production capacity to cater to existing order commitments as well as anticipated future business; total capital expenditure incurred during the year amounted to Rs. 2,437.56 lakhs, financed through a combination of IPO proceeds, term loan and internal accruals. The centrepiece is the second manufacturing facility (Unit 2) at Hanbarwadi in Satara district, Maharashtra - a state-of-the-art greenfield unit developed on 6.5 acres that expands the manufacturing footprint by 50,000 square feet, inaugurated on 20 June 2026 and commencing commercial operations with effect from that date. It is built for complete backward integration and is equipped with robotic welding, laser cutting, bending, a paint shop and modern shot blast; the individual investments listed for the year include installation of a laser cutting machine, a bending machine, heavy-duty cranes and a paint shop at Unit 2, plus construction and installation of a shot blasting shed. Separately the Company renovated its Corporate Office at Unit 1 - Virvade to improve workplace infrastructure and administrative facilities. Management expects these investments to substantially enhance manufacturing capacity, improve operational efficiency, optimise production costs and support long-term strategic objectives. The expansion is framed as a green build - the new manufacturing facility is being developed to meet IGBC Green Building standards with a focus on efficient resource use and responsible construction, alongside energy-efficiency measures and an energy management strategy guided by five tenets, while the Company is still evaluating feasible options for alternate sources of energy (capital investment on energy conservation equipment is not separately indicated as it forms part of other substantive capital assets). Adjacent to the physical build-out, wholly owned subsidiary Trezor Technologies Private Limited entered into an agreement with Smardt Chillers Pte. Ltd., Singapore for the sale, installation and after-sales servicing of chillers to data centres in India, which is expected to strengthen the Company's presence in the data centre cooling segment. The capacity build is backed by a closing order book of over Rs 270 Crore, stated at approximately 1.8x of FY26 revenue.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Stay a defence-focused, Atmanirbhar-aligned engineering company: deepen the niche naval HVAC&R position by strengthening long-term relationships within the defence ecosystem and expanding execution capabilities across specialised naval applications.
- Expand manufacturing capacity through the new Hanbarwadi (Unit 2) greenfield plant with complete backward integration - robotic welding, laser cutting, bending, paint shop, shot blast - to serve existing order commitments and anticipated future business, improve operational efficiency and optimise production costs.

hero.oneLiner: Shree Refrigerations Limited is an Indian engineering company making air-conditioning and turnkey HVAC&R cooling solutions for mission-critical defence, marine and industrial applications, with around 35 years of experience in refrigeration and a defence-led pivot behind its recent growth.
